publisher: Canadian Center of Science and Education
authors: Cleide Maria Diniz Pereira da Silva e Silva
title: Drying of Clay Slabs during the Falling Rate Period: Optimization and Simulation of the Process Using Diffusion Models
scope: Methods 2.1–2.2, 2.7; equations 3, 6, 7; Tables 1, 2, 4. Author-uploaded body text read through web tool; original publisher PDF bytes unavailable.
supports: Falling-rate diffusion model separates internal D from surface coefficient h. Time terms exp[-mu_n^2 D t/(L/2)^2], Bi=h(L/2)/D. Assumptions: fixed thickness, uniform initial moisture, homogeneous isotropic body, constant parameters, diffusion-only interior.

conditions.materialPreparation: 110 C drying, ball-milled, 180 micrometre sieve, extruded; approximately 0.11 kg/kg dry initial water
conditions.ambientRoom: 25 C, 75% RH; not asserted to equal heated drying-air RH

doesNotVerify: No island pot calibration: approximately 6 mm hot-air slabs, no capacity or coil joins; raw time-series CSV, repetition count, and controlled air velocity not acquired. Thickness-squared scaling requires constant dimensionless boundary behavior; fixed h changes Bi when L changes.

evidence.shortExcerpt: the thickness Lx does not vary during drying
